subjective.citation_text: Patient: Hi, I'm Jacqueline. I'm not sure about my exact age, but I'm in my late twenties. I came in because I injured my ankle while mountain biking. It's been hurting a lot, and I can't really walk on it. Doctor: Can you describe the mechanism of injury in more detail, such as how the injury occurred during mountain biking, and have you experienced any swelling, bruising, deformity, or inability to bear weight on the affected ankle? Patient: Sure. So I was in a mountain biking lesson, and I fell off my bike. My right ankle twisted outward, and I heard a crack or a crackle when it happened. Since then, it's been really painful, especially on the outer part of my ankle. I have some bruising and swelling there, and I can't really put any weight on it. It's been a few days now, and I've been limping around. Doctor: Have you experienced any prior ankle injuries or conditions that might affect this current injury? Patient: No, I don't think I've had any prior ankle injuries. I've been mountain biking for about three years, but this is the first time anything like this has happened to my ankle. I don't remember any other issues with it before. Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging or medical evaluations for this injury, such as X-rays, MRI, or a visit to a healthcare provider? Patient: No, I haven't had any imaging or medical evaluations for this injury yet. The doctor just did an exam and ordered an X-ray, and I was told there's no acute fracture, just a soft tissue injury. I'm still waiting on the results and the treatment plan. Doctor: Could you please provide the results of the X-ray that was ordered? If they are not available yet, when can you expect to receive them? Patient: The X-ray results were reviewed by the doctor before they came in, and they said there's no acute fracture
